design_rationale: Rework round 2. One Premier cardholder, two losses on the same account. In August her card was stolen; a foreign online purchase was disputed by phone on the report day, the written confirmation never came, so no provisional credit was owed; it was resolved with an error found on 2026-10-09 and its final credit is still owed (228.62). In September her replacement card went missing (learned 2026-09-08, reported late on 2026-09-14); the September 11 withdrawal claim was signed on 2026-09-23 and provisionally credited with 50.00 withheld, then resolved with an error found on 2026-10-07 with the late-report liability, so the part of its provisional credit above its due must be reversed (415.51). On 2026-10-13 she reported a second withdrawal of that loss by phone; today she signs its written statement (root, owner user, 90.70). Tree: signed claim credit <- (state gate: the other claim of the same loss carries its reversal) reversal <- (value input: available balance; final credits owed on other lost or stolen card claims post first) final credit. Factors are the real dimensions of these credits: Visa Zero Liability vs the timely/late Regulation E limits, liability already charged on the same loss, Paystride fees on the claimed transaction or the free withdrawal it used, the service, late-credit and investigation allowances of the Premier and Elite claim schedules, replacement card fees by loss type, and the early pay the worker had to send to an outside destination on the report day while the card was blocked (Access ledger and tier).
user_scenario: You are Marisol Trask, a 36-year-old prep cook at Sonoran Table Hospitality in Phoenix who is paid on a Paystride Visa Payroll Card. You are calling on your break, a little tense and short on time. Your card went missing in September; you reported it on September 14 and got a new card. Going through your card history later, you found a second ATM withdrawal of about a hundred dollars on September 12 that was not yours, and you called about it on October 13. The person you spoke to said that before that money could go back on your card you would have to sign a written statement about the claim. That is what you want done today: sign whatever you need to sign and get the money for the September 12 withdrawal back on your card. You have no idea how the credit is worked out. Give your details only when the agent asks for them: your mobile number is 6025550142, the last four digits of your Social Security number are 5381, your date of birth is July 19, 1990, and your ZIP code is 85008. If the agent asks when you realized the card was gone, you say it was September 8, a Tuesday, but you kept thinking it would turn up at home and only called on the 14th, and you admit you should have called sooner. If the agent asks which withdrawal, it is the one on September 12 at the Sunrise Market ATM, a little over a hundred dollars. If the agent asks for the card, the new one ends in 5462. If the agent says other items on your card account have to be settled before this credit can be done, you tell them to go ahead and handle whatever has to be handled; you do not argue about amounts you did not ask about, and if they tell you money is being taken back you sigh and only ask them to make sure it is right. When the agent tells you how much will go back on the card for the September 12 withdrawal, you are disappointed it is not the whole amount, but once they explain why, you accept it. When the agent hands you the statement to sign, you sign it for exactly the claim and the amount the agent gives you, and you read back the confirmation you get. Once the credit shows as posted, you thank the agent and end the call. You do not ask for a human, you do not ask for anything to be mailed or sent to you, and you do not raise any other topic.

base_preconditions.condition: A provisional credit is owed only when the notice arrives within error_notice_outer_limit_days calendar days after the disputed transaction's posted date, or, when later, within error_notice_window_days calendar days after the history access date.
A provisional credit is posted only while the dispute's status is investigating.
A dispute receives at most one provisional credit.

temporal_feasibility.condition: A provisional credit is owed only when the notice arrives within error_notice_outer_limit_days calendar days after the disputed transaction's posted date, or, when later, within error_notice_window_days calendar days after the history access date.

temporal_basis.counting_rule: Calendar days are counted from the day after the posted date or the history access date, and a notice arriving on the last day of either period is timely.

boundary_check.just_before: The withdrawal posted 2026-09-12; notice on 2026-10-13 is day 31 of the 120-day outer limit after posting (and day 29 after the 2026-09-14 history access).
boundary_check.at_boundary: A notice on 2027-01-10, the 120th day after posting, would still be timely (inclusive); one on 2027-01-11 would earn no provisional credit, the 60-day window after the history access having closed on 2026-11-13.

temporal_feasibility.condition: A provisional credit reversal posts only after provisional_reversal_notice_business_days business days have passed since the resolution date.

temporal_basis.counting_rule: Business days are Monday through Friday excluding Federal Reserve holidays, counted from the day after the resolution date.

boundary_check.just_before: The claim was resolved 2026-10-07; the five business days after it are 2026-10-08, 2026-10-09, 2026-10-13, 2026-10-14 and 2026-10-15 (2026-10-12 is a Federal Reserve holiday), so they have passed by today, 2026-10-22.
boundary_check.at_boundary: On 2026-10-15 the fifth business day was still running and no reversal could post; from 2026-10-16 it may.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Locate the caller's worker profile from the mobile number she gives.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Every later read and write needs the customer reference number of the cardholder.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Confirm identity with two matching credentials before discussing the card or moving money.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Identity must be confirmed before account information is discussed or any credit or reversal is booked.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the payroll card account: plan (Premier), status, first deposit date, current available balance.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The plan selects the claim schedules and their limits and fees; the available balance is what a reversal may take.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read every claim on the card: the October phone claim on the September 12 withdrawal awaiting written confirmation, the September 11 claim of the same loss (resolved with an error found, provisional credit posted), the August claim of the earlier stolen card (resolved with an error found, no credit), and the June claim resolved with no error.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The signed claim credit waits on the other claim of the same loss carrying its reversal; that reversal waits on every final credit owed on the account's other lost or stolen card claims (the August claim has none).

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the card ledger: the claimed withdrawals and purchase with their surcharges, surcharge rebates and Paystride fees, the replacement card fees, the provisional credit on the September 11 claim and the June credit and reversal.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Every factor of the three computations rests on these rows: fees and rebates on each claimed transaction, the fees on each replacement order and the provisional credit standing on the September 11 claim.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the employer's Payroll Card Program the account was opened under: package Premier, live.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The card plan, and with it which claim schedules apply, follows the employer's package.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the replacement orders: damaged card in April, stolen card on 2026-08-10 (expedited) and lost card on 2026-09-14 (expedited).
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The replacement ordered on a claim's notice date sets its report day and the replacement card fees and early pay cost counted with it.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the cardholder's Paystride Access plan: tier, status, next payday.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The early pay cost on a lost card is capped at the next-business-day bank fee of the tier the Access plan holds today.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the Access ledger: the instant early pay transfers to an external debit card on 2026-08-10 and 2026-09-14 (report days, card blocked) and their fees.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The early pay cost counted with the August final credit and in the September 11 claim's due is the fee booked on those transfers.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the employer's Access program agreement: live, fee model worker_paid.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Under the worker_paid fee model the instant-transfer fees were the worker's own cost.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the Access earnings lines and period closes behind the early pay transfers.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: The tree is a chain (final credit -> reversal -> signed claim credit) with no parallel edges: the reversal's sentence fixes the final credit first (it raises the balance the reversal can take: 469.98 after it, 241.36 before it), and the signed claim credit's sentence fixes the reversal before it. No two writes are left unordered.

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Without the final credit the balance stays 241.36, so the reversal computes 241.36 instead of 415.51 (limited by the balance), and the final credit row of 228.62 is missing from the terminal state.

Without the reversal the terminal state lacks the 415.51 reversal row against 88866d44-19aa-43af-8e0f-04cfb71660dd and the card balance ends 415.51 higher; the signed claim credit itself still computes 90.70 because the liability already charged is read from the other claim's own fields (state gate).
